description: The keys a rule may use in when:, in three groups: what the work is, who the agent is, and when in its life the rules are put together. ACE owns the keys; ASC fills the values from live data and matches. How the text reaches the agent (a file written at setup, a hook's injected output, an opening message, a CLI argument) is ASC's delivery, not a key. Which keys a start kind supplies is ASC's start-request contract, not here.

keys.description: What kind of work the item is (bug, feature, docs, ...), as each domain's registry classifies it.
Persona of the agent: its charter. Head names are persona values.
The agent's part in one workflow step (producer, reviewer, ...); never a head name.
What kind of session this is.
Model family behind the agent; extended by editing this data.
Agent CLI id (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp).
The moment in the agent's life: its start, or the successor start after a session rotation. Hook-event moments are added here as data only when something composes rules at that moment.

componentScope: No component key. A unit with scope component is owned by its component (owner) and applies like any other rule; its when: is empty (always), which keeps today's repo projection byte-identical. Narrowing by component later adds a key here first.
